arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Lach argued the term person remains unchanged since 1863.
Mr. Stewart argued the law targets deliberate efforts to cheat the government.
Mr. Stewart stated the side that brought the case identified no legitimate ground for exclusion.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The False Claims Act targets fraud against the federal government. The term person remains undefined. The Court must decide if local governments fit this term.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: Cook County wants the Court to exclude local governments from the law.
The government wants the Court to include local governments in the law.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: Cook County argues Congress did not intend to include local governments.
The government argues the law covers all entities that cheat the federal government.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Local governments face financial liability for federal fraud. The law defines who must pay penalties. This case sets the scope of federal fraud enforcement.
